samples.question: The picture contains exactly one dark wire: a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness that winds across the whole picture. The wire never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself; parallel folds of the wire are always separated by clear background. Eight small square ticks are printed on the wire, four orange and four blue, so the two colours are always four and four and counting colours never gives the answer. Every tick is narrower than the wire, so a tick never cuts the wire and the ink runs past it on both sides. Two ticks are neighbours only if you meet them one straight after the other while walking along the wire's own ink; stepping across background, or onto a neighbouring fold, is never a legal step. Exactly one pair of neighbours along the wire has two ticks of the same colour; every other pair of neighbours has two different colours. Straight-line looks are not a guide: the two ticks of the same-coloured pair always sit far apart on the page, and the two same-coloured ticks that look closest together on the page are never that pair. Gray squares near the border are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour is shared by the one pair of neighbouring ticks along the wire that have the same colour? Answer orange or blue.
